title: Implement prefill collection, event-clock calibration and HTTP predictor pilot
body:
This PR implements prefill collection, event-clock calibration and predictor experiments, stacked on #31.

**Latest native attempt at efca3e4 stops at TRAIN readiness: 88 controlled trials complete, three of 24 first-commit checks fail, and no held controlled or HTTP trial is attempted. Original-source offline reconstruction reproduces the rejection.** The earlier 240-trial native confirmation remains a pass on its own host, with identical F0/entry forecasts there. Cross-host robustness is unestablished. Global production model, HTTP, adaptive-cap and MPC acceptance remain false.

### Conditional state timing envelope: CPU prototype

A separate `state-time-envelope-v1` interface now computes lower/upper cut-relative engine times for fixed pre-ADD membership/progress, no later arrivals and forced lengths. Every future batch may independently vary within declared CPU/GPU support. The supported logical two-slot graph is time-independent and max-plus monotone; extremal runs bound its event times under those assumptions. Independent EventGraph checks include varying per-batch services, ready/inflight busy cuts, overlap, TTFT and full completion.

Ready pending work has zero debt without charging its old CPU return again. Unready debt uses the declared effective anchor/support; overdue upper support abstains. Missing/old/mixed-clock inputs remain unavailable. Wide intervals stay visible and require fallback. Runtime, dispatcher, source, support and policy identities are bound. The public point forecast retains its original overdue behavior.

TRAIN-only construction matches the original event identities, then derives empirical prefill/decode ranges from **3280** past prefix host spans: **10.733–55.953ms / 0.738–4.337ms**. GPU coefficients stay at the development fit. These ranges are **not confidence intervals, native coverage estimates or identified physical costs**. All **24** checked legacy release records lack pending/time state and report unavailable; no later ready bit or completion supplies missing inputs. The old 3/24 rejection is unchanged.

**285 related CPU checks plus one metadata/hash check pass (286 total)**, bound to 204 current source files. These overlap previous selections and do not replace the captured 1414-test native acceptance. A standalone CPU CLI builds support/replays snapshots. Optional deadline relations refer only to engine time from the cut; every output keeps actuation, native coverage, online compute-age qualification, model/HTTP/cap/MPC acceptance false.

This is a CPU representation and arithmetic implementation, not a completed native repair. A separately frozen short shadow collection contract/entrypoint is still required to measure fresh coverage, usefulness, unavailable rates, observer effects and actual compute age before another full rental run. No native collector command is added and `entry-http` is not upgraded or unblocked by this prototype.

- [Conditional envelope design and CPU commands](https://github.com/dlinlabs/vllm-serving-lab/blob/13e783c58d499c8d8fda226809eb1915b199ab45/experiments/prefill-state-envelope-v1.md)
- [CPU evidence, empirical support, unavailable inputs and limits](https://github.com/dlinlabs/vllm-serving-lab/blob/13e783c58d499c8d8fda226809eb1915b199ab45/results/prefill-state-envelope-cpu/report.md)

### Native TRAIN rejection and diagnostic repair

Archive `1793156148422216020.tar.gz` (19,833,493 bytes; SHA256 `a281a36e0939a7181233f8c7edbc5dc86bec598cd33377c83a641d26f51e4d8f`) matches all 115 raw files and all 199 captured source files at efca3e4. Its byte-identical native CPU proof passes **1414 tests**, including the five required trace configurations. A verified isolated source tree with captured NumPy2.3.5/SciPy1.18.1 rebuilds the raw prefix, runtime/source/manifest/launch/CPU identities and original TRAIN estimator. It reconstructs a rejection, not complete-collection acceptance.

First-commit readiness passes **21/24** samples. qc-047, qc-060 and qc-070 exceed their original 10ms limits with absolute errors **14.225, 11.242 and 21.795ms**. Phase construction has no errors. The 88-trial controlled prefix takes 406.433s, then stops.

For single-L7168-D16, repeated first commits are **51.639, 50.539, 25.161 and 49.974ms**. Their original acceptable prediction intervals have empty intersection: a common point would need to be >=41.311ms and <=35.161ms. Another fixed-case constant cannot make every repeat pass. Normalized recorded release scheduler states match, but omit pending readiness/debt and physical CPU/GPU state; this does not identify hardware/network/CPU contention or rule out state-conditioned prediction. First commit can consume an earlier background batch; it is not foreground TTFT.

The collector now saves rejected base/candidate documents and exact failed checks under separate diagnostic filenames, then stops. Accepted freeze/seal files remain absent. No sample exclusion, automatic retry, relaxed budget or coefficient change is introduced. **172 related local CPU checks pass, with zero failures/errors/skips**, bound to 201 current source files and separate from the capture's 1414 native cases and earlier local selections. The predictor itself remains unrepaired/unaccepted; next design needs decision-time observable state and/or explicit uncertainty with a separately frozen qualification plan. No new GPU rental is needed to analyze this archive.

- [Rejection results, failed checks, limits and reproduction](https://github.com/dlinlabs/vllm-serving-lab/blob/3b20995e71122a44fd5cc68eeee0938490a2253c/results/prefill-entry-http-train-rejection-efca3e4/report.md)
- [Original-source failure analyzer](https://github.com/dlinlabs/vllm-serving-lab/blob/3b20995e71122a44fd5cc68eeee0938490a2253c/scripts/analyze_prefill_entry_http_failure.py)

### Entry-return HTTP integration

The new `entry-http` host operation runs 240 fresh controlled trials followed by the original 98-case HTTP design in a separate namespace. It requires a passing same-host controlled prerequisite; carries the frozen six-term GPU lane and prefill/decode CPU-return constants into pre-ADD busy-state prediction; and seals the model and TRAIN-only transport correction before held HTTP outcomes. Pending CPU return is not charged twice and overlaps GPU service.

The handoff binds source, runtime, boot/time namespace, both manifests, the original controlled report and freeze, chronology and native acknowledgement. Every native forecast records the configuration identity. The independent checker rebuilds the controlled sub-audit, model handoff, client/gateway/native joins, work sequence, forecast, transport seal, scores, request totals and closed telemetry from raw evidence. Failures and cancellation retain partial captures and archives without automatic retries. Old standalone confirmation and `live-http` contracts remain separate.

Engine max(10ms,20%), HTTP max(15ms,20%), observer max(2ms,10%), snapshot <=1ms, forecast age <=5ms and TRAIN transport spread <=10ms remain unchanged. The combined 3600s collection bound does not include setup/full native CPU acceptance/startup/final audit. A separate offline F0 replay uses identical LIGHT snapshots; it cannot select a model from held outcomes or establish causal performance gain.

### CPU validation and limits

The original integration proof at **ce01ad8** has **348 related CPU tests passing in 93.85s, with zero failures, errors or skips.** The committed validation report records the exact selection, JUnit, logs and all 199 source-file hashes. Tests cover independent EventGraph parity from empty and busy states, CPU/GPU overlap, pending work, native configuration, launch-mode conflicts, resealed handoff tampering, both manifest paths, all 98 HTTP stages, prerequisite/warmup/generator/cancellation failures, and raw-audit evidence tampering. These are local CPU/mock/synthetic checks, not a new full native acceptance run or native HTTP accuracy result.

The pre-ADD observation occurs after admission. Known client-to-cut time does not make this a predictor available before admission, and fixed protected32 does not qualify the cost-aware admission-budget action path.

### Slow-download setup recovery

The fixed 1800s dependency-install cutoff interrupted a rental download before collection. Setup now accepts `--install-timeout SECONDS` (default 7200), keeps the current venv/cache and stops before acceptance/collection on timeout. Completed cached files may be reused; partial downloads may restart. This does not increase network speed or change the 3600s collection bound or accuracy gates. **71 related local CPU/mock checks pass in 4.65s**, separately scoped from the original 348-case integration proof at ce01ad8. The later efca3e4 capture completes installation and reaches controlled TRAIN; HTTP remains unattempted. [Recovery proof](https://github.com/dlinlabs/vllm-serving-lab/blob/experiments/prefill-service-design-v1/results/prefill-setup-timeout-cpu/report.md).

### Historical native evidence retained unchanged

Archive `1793136029888154788.tar.gz`, SHA256 `c569e2d78ccefdab3ecc8d275181bb320c07f51ba6e983a5fdd1b7e7027858b5`: all 260 raw files and 191 captured source files match commit **2ebb185**, including its byte-identical **1331-test native CPU acceptance**. The original source-bound strict audit is independently reproduced with matching NumPy2.3.5/SciPy1.18.1; no equality rule, source guard or error budget is relaxed.

All 240 native trials complete in 1003.371s. All 144 held queue samples pass the original max(10ms,20%) budget. Baseline OFF queue MAE/max are 1.920/4.940ms. All 48 comparable receipt/LIGHT controls, endpoint, before/after anchor and work/lifetime gates pass. All eight cells have one TRAIN-eligible branch and exactly identical F0/entry predictions. This does not prove a correction advantage, cross-host robustness or resolution of the earlier host's phase switch. Older failed-run verdicts and ablations remain unchanged.

### Bounded path to MPC

The roadmap distinguishes engine B2048, protected concurrency32, background D16 and the weighted cost-aware budget **C16/C32**. The authenticated `/admin/budget` actuator already exists. Remaining gates are (1) native HTTP state-bridge qualification, (2) separately qualified cost-aware decision state and held action/drain ranking across C16/C32, then (3) a minimal receding-horizon loop compared against replicated fixed16/fixed32 and a myopic/hysteresis baseline. Gate2 CPU design can proceed without inserting an open-ended production calibration stage.

Cap reduction lets existing requests finish and rejects new offers while weighted admitted cost exceeds the budget; it does not cancel requests or create a waiting queue. Future EOS and recorded future Azure arrivals cannot be oracle controller inputs. If one fixed cap consistently wins, report that result rather than asserting an MPC benefit.
